Hypothesis: H1. Delay rises non linearly with load and backlog
Evidence: TWFE on N = 100 ministry months. Backlog ratio +25.013 days (p = 0.0005), squared term -9.62 (p = 0.0069).
Verdict: Supported for backlog. Load per active GRO is not a congestion driver once ministry effects are held.

Hypothesis: H2. Ministry differences persist after load
Evidence: Ministry effects lift R2 of ATR share from 0.782 to 0.9727 (+19.06 pp), N = 115.
Verdict: Supported. Process and practice differ by ministry.

Hypothesis: H3. Pooling cuts delay at equal capacity
Evidence: M/M/1 vs M/M/2 cuts wait 52.6 to 89.7 percent. With calibrated Cs2 = 2.64 the safe utilisation ceiling rises from 0.601 (1 desk) to 0.877 (4 desks).
Verdict: Supported analytically with service time variability calibrated from DARPG ageing data.

Evidence: Interrupted time series on Little's Law W. Level shift -4.484 days (p = 0.0208) after Aug 2024, slope change +1.172 (p = 0.008).
Verdict: Partly supported. One time drop in mean time, no lasting change in the aged tail.

Hypothesis: H5. Citizen perceived timeliness lags reported timeliness
Evidence: Call centre 2026. 40.94 percent confirm resolution, true satisfaction 32.72 percent. Citizen cohort substantive resolution 8.3 percent.
Verdict: Supported by both secondary and primary evidence.
